title: Effect of Dry Needling Plus Vibration on Myofascial Trigger Points in Individuals With Nonspecific Low Back Pain
official: Effectiveness and Acceptability of Adding a Percutaneous Vibratory Stimulus to Dry Needling for the Treatment of Myofascial Trigger Points in Individuals With Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Randomized Non-Inferiority Trial
summary:
This study evaluates whether adding mechanical vibration to dry needling (DN+V) is not inferior to dry needling alone (DN) for reducing low back pain intensity in adults with nonspecific low back pain (NSLBP), when both interventions are combined with a structured exercise program.

The primary hypothesis is non-inferiority in pain reduction (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, NPRS) at 1 week after treatment, using a non-inferiority margin of 1 point on the 0-10 NPRS scale. If non-inferiority is confirmed, secondary analyses will explore whether DN+V is superior to DN alone in patient-reported treatment acceptability, pain experienced during the intervention, and post-needling soreness.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two parallel groups: DN plus exercise, or DN+V plus exercise. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at multiple time points up to 4 weeks after treatment, including pain intensity, disability, acceptability, muscle strength, pressure pain threshold, quality of life, and global impression of change. Direct and indirect costs associated with both interventions will also be collected to provide data for a future economic evaluation of the cost-effectiveness of DN+V compared with DN.
